notes: '[bʷˠ] is a voiced allophone of /pʷˠ/ and occurs intervocalically' ([sɛbʷˠato] 'Saturday') (p. 19).

A velar fricative [x], 'which I believe to be an allophone of /g/'; heard word-initially, medially and finally, the environment not predictable. Some speakers said [k], [g] and [x] could be interchangeable (p. 21).
'[l] is an allophone of /n/, since either can be used in a word with no change in meaning' (Jackson 1983: 163); perhaps from the influence of neighbouring languages with both l and n (pp. 23-24).

'a → e / ___Ca' (written with e): a morphophonemic rule, as in /saːm/ 'father' but /sɛmaɻ/ before the 1st person exclusive suffix; no longer productive, since aCa occurs within words (/asam/ 'door') (pp. 30-31).
